providers.name: Leray spectral sequence
providers.proof_locus: Section 4; current sheaf-operations course, derived pullback and pushforward, Proposition 3.1 and Exercise 3.
providers.conditions: Any morphism of ringed spaces and any module sheaf in degree zero; first quadrant, finite filtration in every total degree. No finite dimension, separation or properness assumption.

providers.name: Affine quasi-coherent vanishing
providers.proof_locus: Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 2.2; Čech lesson, Theorem 4.1.
providers.conditions: Every ring R and every R-module M; H^p(Spec R, tilde M)=0 for p>0. No Noetherian or finite-generation assumption.

providers.name: Serre’s affine criterion
providers.proof_locus: Lemma 5.1 and Theorem 5.2; affine vanishing in Theorem 2.2.
providers.conditions: X quasi-compact; affineness is equivalent to vanishing of all positive quasi-coherent cohomology, and to H^1(X,I)=0 for every quasi-coherent ideal. The statement does not require quasi-separatedness.

providers.name: Serre’s theorems on projective space
providers.proof_locus: Proposition 1.2; descending induction in Theorem 2.1; preceding projective-space lesson, Theorem 2.2.
providers.conditions: R Noetherian, F coherent on P_R^N; finite cohomology, eventual higher-twist vanishing and eventual global generation.

providers.name: Serre’s theorems for a proper scheme with an ample line bundle
providers.proof_locus: Lemma 1.3 proves the closed embedding; Theorems 2.1–2.2, with the finite residue-class argument.
providers.conditions: X proper over a Noetherian affine base R, F coherent and L ample; finiteness, and vanishing and global generation for every sufficiently large integer twist. Thresholds on a merely locally Noetherian non-quasi-compact base are only local.

providers.name: Flat base change
providers.proof_locus: Section 1 constructs the canonical map; Section 2 proves the separated case and the finite spectral-sequence comparison for quasi-separated X.
providers.conditions: f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, F quasi-coherent, g flat; every higher direct-image comparison is an isomorphism. F need not be flat. Includes localization and nonseparated X.

providers.name: Fiber vanishing gives locally free H^0 and arbitrary base change
providers.proof_locus: Lemma 2.1 and Corollary 5.3 prove the fiber-vanishing case. Corollary 5.1 proves the higher-direct-image-vanishing case. Lesson 8 proves the Noetherian finite model; Lemma 0.1 of lesson9 writes the general-base finite model using exact earlier finite-presentation and flatness proofs. Constant fiber dimension alone on a nonreduced base is insufficient; Theorem 4.1 assumes a reduced base.
providers.conditions: Noetherian base: f proper, F coherent and base-flat. Arbitrary base: f proper of finite presentation, F finitely presented and base-flat. All positive fiber cohomology vanishes at every point. Then f_*F is finite locally free, all positive higher direct images vanish, and both assertions commute with arbitrary base change. No reducedness is required. A line bundle on a flat proper finitely presented family satisfies the sheaf conditions.

providers.name: Formal functions
providers.proof_locus: Sections 2–4, especially Lemma 2.2, Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 4.1. Corollary 4.2 gives the locally Noetherian stalk form using lesson 8 localization.
providers.conditions: A Noetherian, I any ideal, X proper over Spec A, F coherent; the canonical I-adic completed cohomology is the inverse limit of cohomology on X_n. F need not be flat and A need not be complete.

providers.name: Cohen–Macaulay projective Serre duality
providers.proof_locus: Sections 2–4; local Ext vanishing, ambient projective-space duality from lesson 14 and Theorem 4.2. Local algebra inputs are recorded separately.
providers.conditions: X projective over a field k, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional of dimension n, F coherent; Ext_X^(n-i)(F,omega_X) is naturally dual to H^i(X,F), for every integer i. For a smooth projective equidimensional curve and invertible L this gives H^1(L)^vee=H^0(omega_X tensor L^-1). No non-Cohen–Macaulay sheaf-duality extension is asserted.
